rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notices, grounds)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict or fail to renew a residential lease without good cause. Except for nonpayment of rent, a written Notice to Quit (with detailed cause, and often a prior Notice to Cease) is required before filing; notice periods range from 3 days to 3 years depending on the ground. Self-help evictions and lockouts are illegal.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years depending on ground

unverifiable_exemptions: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units
unit held in trust for developmentally disabled family member

rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, apartments, mobile homes, rooming and boarding houses.
rules.exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient/seasonal hotel and motel guests; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member.
rules.penalty: Tenant illegally evicted may recover possession and damages including court costs and attorney fees.

parsed.doc_summary: Part 3 of the NJ DCA landlord-tenant handbook. It covers habitability, heat, lead and water disclosures, and the Anti-Eviction Act (good cause, notice to quit, grounds, self-help bans, relocation). Only the eviction material falls in the listed categories, so I extracted one just-cause record. The part cuts off mid-section on the drug-offense ground.
